Computer Occupations, All Other

About the Role
All computer occupations not listed separately.
What You'll Do
Monitor systems for intrusions or denial of service attacks, and report security breaches to appropriate personnel.
Identify or document backup or recovery plans.
Back up or modify applications and related data to provide for disaster recovery.
Correct testing-identified problems, or recommend actions for their resolution.
Identify, standardize, and communicate levels of access and security.
Determine sources of Web page or server problems, and take action to correct such problems.
Implement updates, upgrades, and patches in a timely manner to limit loss of service.
Implement Web site security measures, such as firewalls or message encryption.
Collaborate with development teams to discuss, analyze, or resolve usability issues.
Test issues such as system integration, performance, and system security on a regular schedule or after any major program modifications.


Tools & Technology
Document management software: Adobe Acrobat
Development environment software: Adobe ActionScript, Apache Ant
Web platform development software: Adobe ColdFusion, AJAX, Apache Struts, Apache Tomcat
Graphics or photo imaging software: Adobe Creative Cloud software, Adobe FreeHand MX, Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Photoshop
Video creation and editing software: Adobe Director
Web page creation and editing software: Adobe Dreamweaver, Adobe Experience Manager (AEM), Adobe Macromedia HomeSite
Desktop publishing software: Adobe InDesign, Adobe PageMaker
Data base user interface and query software: Amazon Web Services AWS software
Application server software: Apache HTTP Server
Internet browser software: Apple Safari
Education & Experience
Education: Bachelor's degree or Post-secondary certificate or Associate's degree
On-the-Job Training: Up to 1 month
Related Work Experience: 4 years to 6 years
Work Environment
E-Mail
Spend Time Sitting
Indoors, Environmentally Controlled
Telephone Conversations
